name: Miracles
essenceStatement: The Spirit's power producing acts that exceed the ordinary course of nature, given for the body's good and the glory of God.
workingDefinition: The Spirit-given empowerment for the believer to be the means through which God acts in ways that exceed the ordinary course of nature. Paul's word in 1 Corinthians 12:10 is energemata dynameon -- 'workings of powers.' The gift is broader than healing and encompasses any moment when the Spirit's power produces what natural means cannot. As with healing, the power is God's; the gift is the believer's role. The gift is real, attested throughout church history, and never formulaic.
diagnosticChallenge: The contemporary church has split sharply on this gift. Cessationist traditions have argued that the miraculous gifts ceased with the apostolic era. Charismatic traditions have sometimes inflated normal answered prayer into 'miracle' language, diluting the category. The instrument's position is the continuationist one: miracles continue, they are rare, they are sovereign, and they cannot be produced by technique or formula. The diagnostic question is whether the believer has been the means through which acts have occurred that cannot be explained by ordinary providence -- and whether those acts have produced glory for God and good for the body.

manifestationWitnesses.text: But Peter put them all outside, and knelt down and prayed; and turning to the body he said, 'Tabitha, arise.' And she opened her eyes, and when she saw Peter she sat up... He gave her his hand and raised her up. Then, calling the saints and widows, he presented her alive.
manifestationWitnesses.note: Peter and Tabitha -- the gift of miracles in its sharpest biblical form: the dead raised. Peter knelt and prayed before speaking; the action followed the seeking of God. The miracle confirmed the gospel in Joppa and brought many to faith. The gift functions for the body's good and God's glory, not for the spectacle of the miracle itself.

manifestationWitnesses.text: And God was doing extraordinary miracles by the hands of Paul, so that even handkerchiefs or aprons that had touched his skin were carried away to the sick, and their diseases left them and the evil spirits came out of them.
manifestationWitnesses.note: Paul at Ephesus -- the gift of miracles in sustained operation through a single believer's ministry. Note Luke's careful phrasing: 'God was doing.' The power was God's. Paul was the means.

stewardshipCharge.text: ...how shall we escape if we neglect such a great salvation? It was declared at first by the Lord, and it was attested to us by those who heard, while God also bore witness by signs and wonders and various miracles and by gifts of the Holy Spirit distributed according to his will.
stewardshipCharge.note: The author of Hebrews ties miracles directly to God's bearing witness to the gospel. The gift exists to confirm the message of Christ, not to produce a parallel ministry of supernatural display. The miracles point to Christ; the gift is properly exercised only when Christ is being preached and the church is being built up.

inclinationQuestions: I have seen specific events occur in answer to prayer or in the course of my obedience to God that cannot be explained by coincidence, providence, or ordinary outcomes -- and those events occurred in ways that involved me in some specific role.

When I pray for situations that seem impossible by natural means, I find that the Spirit gives me a settled confidence that God is going to act, and that confidence proves accurate more often than chance would explain.

People in my circle have testified that God acted in their circumstances in ways that exceeded ordinary providence, and that what they experienced was tied in some way to my prayer or my obedience to a Spirit-given prompting.
fruitfulnessQuestion: How often have you been involved in -- through prayer, obedience to a Spirit-given prompting, or some specific action -- events that cannot be explained by ordinary providence and that pointed observably to God's hand?
communityConfirmationQuestion: [Name] is connected to events I have observed -- through their prayer, their obedience, or some specific action they took -- that cannot be explained by ordinary providence and that pointed clearly to God's hand.

bodyApplication.where: Miracles function in evangelistic contexts (often in cross-cultural mission work where the gospel is encountering territory that has not heard it), in moments of acute spiritual warfare, in prayer for the impossible, and in seasons of unusual Kingdom advance. They tend to cluster around the spread of the gospel rather than around the personal needs of established believers. Paul's miracles at Ephesus were in the context of breakthrough evangelism, not personal benefit.
bodyApplication.whatItLooksLike: The believer through whom God acts powerfully but who consistently directs attention back to Christ. The missionary who reports the impossible thing that happened, then continues preaching the gospel without inflating the story. The intercessor whose prayers seem to break through situations others have written off. A miracles-gifted believer functioning well is suspicious of platform, careful with testimony, and quick to attribute everything to God. The miracle is a sign, not a destination.
bodyApplication.distortions: The most damaging distortion is the construction of 'miracle ministry' as a brand or product, with curated testimonies, paid conferences, and financial appeals tied to the promise of supernatural breakthrough. It can become showmanship -- the dramatic performance with no real fruit beyond the moment. It can become the inflation of normal answered prayer into 'miracle' language, which dilutes the category and trains the body to expect supernatural intervention in situations where ordinary providence is sufficient. The gift, when divorced from accountability and from the proclamation of Christ, becomes spiritual entertainment.
bodyApplication.pairings: Miracles function alongside Faith and Healing -- the three manifestation gifts that consistently cluster together in scripture and in church history. The miracles-gifted believer typically also carries faith and often healing. The gift also pairs naturally with Evangelism, since the New Testament pattern is for miracles to attend the proclamation of the gospel rather than to function as their own ministry.

formationOutput.active:
The Spirit's work through you in the gift of miracles is to be the means through whom God acts powerfully -- often in moments of spiritual breakthrough, evangelistic advance, or response to specific Spirit-given direction. This is what Peter exhibited with Tabitha and what God did through Paul at Ephesus. The power is always God's. The gift is your role in the moment.

The stewardship of this gift is among the most demanding in the New Testament. Hebrews 2 ties miracles directly to the bearing witness to Christ. The gift is properly exercised when Christ is being preached and the church is being built up, and improperly exercised when it becomes its own destination. The miracles-gifted believer must guard their heart against platform, against the inflation of stories, against the slow drift into spiritual entertainment, and against any teaching that puts the burden of breakthrough on the recipient's faith rather than on God's sovereignty.
formationOutput.anchorScriptureText: God also bore witness by signs and wonders and various miracles and by gifts of the Holy Spirit distributed according to his will.
formationOutput.weeklyPractice: This week, identify one situation in your life or your community that would require God to act -- a relational impasse that human effort cannot resolve, a financial need that natural means cannot meet, a spiritual breakthrough that ordinary witness has not produced. Pray for it daily. Be ready to act in obedience if the Spirit prompts you. Do not announce what you are praying for. If God acts, tell the story carefully and point only to him. The gift of miracles is not performed; it is received.

edgeCases.emerging: Your responses suggest the Spirit may be developing this gift in you, but the consistent, observable fruit that the New Testament associates with the gift has not yet been confirmed in your community. This is a gift that develops slowly, often over many years, in the context of sustained prayer and faithful witness to Christ. Find a more seasoned, accountable believer or pastor who has seen God act powerfully and submit your sense of this gift to their oversight. Be wary of any teaching that promises breakthrough through technique. The gift, if it is real, will emerge as God acts -- not as you produce.
edgeCases.inclinationConfirmationGap: You sense the Spirit's power moving in connection with your prayer or obedience, but the people who know you well have not seen consistent fruit that they would call miraculous. This is one of the most important findings the instrument can surface, because the gift of miracles is highly vulnerable to self-deception -- internal sensations during prayer or moments of perceived breakthrough can feel like Spirit-given power without producing the verifiable, attested fruit that scripture associates with the gift. Submit your sense of this gift to careful, accountable testing. Trust the witness of the body over the witness of your own impressions.
edgeCases.confirmationInclinationGap: Two or more of the people who weighed in see the gift of miracles working through you in ways you did not claim. The believer who carries this gift often does not name it as such -- they simply pray, obey, and watch God act. Worth taking seriously. Submit this finding to your pastor or a trusted elder. Pay attention in the coming weeks to the moments when God seems to act in connection with your prayer or your obedience. The gift functions best within the structure of a local church under accountable leadership.
edgeCases.quiet: This gift is not where the Spirit is most visibly working through you in this season. That is information, not deficiency. The gift of miracles is given according to the Spirit's will, and its absence in a believer's life is no commentary on their faithfulness or maturity. Every believer is called to pray for the impossible and to trust God for what only he can do. Trust the miracles-gifted believers in your community when they emerge, and look to the gifts where the Spirit is more clearly at work in you.
